questions.learningObjective: Compare velocity across economies
questions.stem: Stage one: economy A has higher money demand than economy B; stage two: with equal spending, which has lower velocity?

options.text: Both equal, since spending is equal
Economy B, since lower demand means more turnover
Economy A, since higher demand means a larger money stock
Neither, since velocity is policy-fixed

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain price-level effect on nominal demand
questions.stem: If all prices double while real income and rates are unchanged, nominal money demand?

options.text: Quadruples, because prices and income both scale
options.misconception: adds an income change not stated

options.text: Stays the same, because real income is unchanged
Halves, because money buys less
Doubles, because each transaction needs twice as many money units

questions.explanation: Nominal demand scales with prices when real income and rates are fixed; a price doubling doubles nominal demand.

questions.learningObjective: Identify an inflation hedge
questions.stem: A table compares cash, gold, and an indexed bond under 6 percent inflation; which best preserves real value?

options.text: Cash, since it is the most liquid asset
The indexed bond, since its payments adjust with inflation
Gold, since it always appreciates faster than inflation
None, since inflation erodes all assets

questions.explanation: Indexed payments adjust with inflation, preserving real value; cash erodes and gold is not guaranteed.

questions.topic: Central bank balance sheet and open market operations
questions.learningObjective: Explain OMO transmission to money supply
questions.stem: Explain the chain from an open market purchase to a larger money supply.

answer.exemplar: The purchase raises bank reserves, creating excess reserves that banks lend; new deposits form and are partly relent, multiplying the initial reserve injection into a larger money supply.

questions.explanation: Reserve injection creates excess reserves, lending creates deposits, and repeated lending multiplies the effect.

questions.learningObjective: Summarize money demand determinants
questions.stem: Stage one: prices, income, and rates all change; stage two: nominal money demand is determined by?

options.text: Income alone, since transactions drive demand
Prices alone, since nominal demand only tracks prices
All three, since prices scale nominal demand and income and rates shape real demand
Rates alone, since opportunity cost dominates
